Current scoped evidence does not justify rollback.

retention_decision.limit: Earlier cancellation observations and unchanged reader files do not prove an identical cause, a benign cancellation or full customer acceptance. Strict aggregates remain false and per-request stream/UI correlation stays open.

selected_code_review.proposed_job: Effect-free projection of a saved Poly Haven asset-list snapshot into existing knowledge_radar Observation and SourceCheck records, preserving native identity, actual zeroes, unknown fields and capture provenance.

retained_failed_attempts: The first planning run passed 97 of 99 tests; generated continuation output became stale after review edits. Regeneration, both failed-case reruns and the full 99-case successor passed; the original result remains.

The initial regeneration command exited zero while its conformance report still had all_gates_pass=false. A narrow registration of passive urllib.parse use repaired the boundary; the successor passed without generated-byte drift.

The first full pre-push run passed 17 of 20 gates. Tool group c had five errors and one skip in 1,341 cases; group d had two failures and one skip in 1,239. Group a's 1,058 cases and group b's 1,141 passed with six and one skips. Short/long temporary-path controls isolated the fixture boundary; the exact candidate's successor passed all 20 gates. Chrome's internal SIGTRAP cause was not established.

The hardcoding audit's single new high finding was the exact admitted HTTPS redirect Location. One independently reviewed expiring exception was recorded; the complete follow-up audit reported zero blocking findings.

Offline live-checker preparation found encoded-path exclusion, redirect-interception, WebSocket-interception, incomplete export-provenance and empty Set-Cookie checks that needed repair. A later HTTP-status observer control proved that 404, 500 and 401 snapshots survive request completion and a later 200. Original probes remain beside passing successors.

Deployment attempt 1 failed at authority before any checkout or provider/service effect. Fresh reconciliation retained release 92 and a closed gate before the separately recorded successful attempt 2.

Edge attempt 1 completed its local export but failed on the pinned MCP result-field mismatch before any provider write. GET-only reconciliation confirmed the prior deployment, export and settings unchanged; original source and journal remain.

Edge attempt 2's Worker PUT was acknowledged, then its postcheck failed by comparing different identity types. No repeat PUT occurred. Separate GET-only deployment, version and settings readback confirmed the intended deployment while retaining the original failed verifier.

Public matrix attempt 1 completed 1 of 20 hosts and 6 of 200 views, with 19 of 20 assertions and four error entries for three native fetch failures plus their aggregate. It recorded no instrumentation or body-read errors, but the fetch root cause is unknown. Later successful Node GET and curl HEAD probes remain separate; attempt 2 used the same frozen checker and manifest with new output after asset readback.

Public matrix attempt 2 completed all 20 hosts and 200 views but passed 4,711 of 4,715 assertions and retained 21 canceled HTTP200 metadata-fetch errors and accounting events. Four AgentFeeds checks used the wrong source contract; a preserved successor corrects that expectation without changing production code or suppressing metadata-fetch failures.

The initial metadata-fetch fixture diagnosis passed 12 of 14 controls; navigation hypotheses were not reproduced. A separate exact-guard comparison passed 8 of 8. Neither established the production cause or a benign attribution. All results remain available for the existing website owners.

Public matrix attempt 3 completed all 20 hosts, 200 views and 4,715 assertions, but retained 21 canceled HTTP200 metadata-fetch errors and the same 21 accounting events. No HTTP response of 400 or higher or native body-read error was recorded. Functional, accounting and strict results remain false; all three matrix reports are preserved.
scope_limits: Application health, reconciled edge deployment, exact public-asset readback, the 118 redirect probes and all 4,715 final assertions qualify the narrow public redirect scope only. The final matrix's metadata-fetch errors keep the broader browser/customer journey unqualified.
No host configuration, DNS, catalogue publication, model, billing or social-publishing change is part of this application release.
Public-page canonical redirects do not migrate www browser storage or prove complete authenticated navigation continuity. Protocol, OAuth and stateful-route exclusions retain separate qualification.
The signed-out public QA profile refuses unreviewed socket and worker transports as functional failures. It is not a general browser sandbox or a qualification of media engines.
History review covered available conversation narrative and recovered oversized user text, not every generated source file, historical media artifact or truncated tool payload.
AgentBriefs purchase is owner-confirmed; registrar, DNS and launch qualification are separate. Source access and inventory completeness do not establish redistribution rights.
Release 92 reports and their false strict aggregates remain unchanged.
